## Summary

**The needle:** an off-by-one in the quorum check in `app/cluster/node.go`.

```go
// before
if finalVotes >= totalNodes/2 {   // 2 >= 2 → minority wins
// after
if finalVotes > totalNodes/2 {     // needs > half → true majority
```

With a 5-node cluster, `totalNodes/2` is `2` (integer division). The old `>=` let a candidate become leader with only **2 votes**, so the minority partition `[0,1]` (node 0 + node 1) could elect a leader at the same time as the majority partition `[2,3,4]` — a split-brain. A real quorum requires *strictly more than* half, i.e. 3 of 5.

Now only the majority partition (node 2, with 3 votes) becomes leader; node 0 with 2 votes correctly stays a candidate. `test.sh` passes all 3 rounds: **PASS: No split-brain detected across all rounds**.

Note: I couldn't overwrite the root-owned `/usr/local/bin/split-brain`, so I rebuilt to `/tmp/bin` and ran the test with that on `PATH`. The source fix is committed to the working tree; a normal container rebuild (the Dockerfile compiles from `app/`) will pick it up.

The test passes: **`PASS: No split-brain detected across all rounds`**.

## The needle

`app/cluster/node.go:124` — the quorum check used a `>=` where it needed `>`:

```go
if finalVotes >= totalNodes/2 {   // bug
```

For a 5-node cluster, `totalNodes/2` is `2` (integer division). The `>=` comparison meant a candidate winning just **2** votes became leader. Under the `[0,1] | [2,3,4]` partition, the minority side (node 0 + node 1 = 2 votes) cleared the bar at the same time as the majority side (node 2 with 3 votes) — two simultaneous leaders, i.e. split-brain.

## The fix

A majority quorum requires *strictly more than half* the nodes:

```go
if finalVotes > totalNodes/2 {    // needs ≥3 of 5
```

Now the 2-node minority partition falls short (`2 > 2` is false) and never elects a leader, while the 3-node majority still succeeds — the single-leader invariant holds.

Note: the on-PATH `/usr/local/bin/split-brain` is root-owned and couldn't be overwritten, so I ran the test against the rebuilt binary via `PATH="/tmp:$PATH"`. In the normal build path (the Dockerfile), the corrected source compiles straight into the image binary.

## The needle

In `/app/app/cluster/node.go`, the quorum check in `StartElection`:

```go
if finalVotes >= totalNodes/2 {   // BUG
```

For a 5-node cluster, `totalNodes/2` is `2` (integer division truncates). The `>=` then lets any candidate with **2 or more** votes become leader. Under the `[0,1] | [2,3,4]` partition:
- Partition B (`[2,3,4]`): node 2 gets 3 votes → leader (legitimately, it's the majority).
- Partition A (`[0,1]`): node 0 gets exactly 2 votes (itself + node 1) → `2 >= 2` → **also becomes leader**. Two leaders = split-brain.

A correct majority quorum needs *strictly more* than half the cluster (3 of 5). The fix:

```go
if finalVotes > totalNodes/2 {   // strict majority: 3 for a 5-node cluster
```

Now `2 > 2` is false, so the minority partition can never elect a leader, while the majority partition (`3 > 2`) still can.

## Verification

I rebuilt the binary and ran `test.sh`. All 3 rounds pass:

```

Round 3: OK
PASS: No split-brain detected across all rounds
```

One note: the installed `/usr/local/bin/split-brain` is owned by root and I lack write access (no sudo), so I couldn't overwrite it in place. I built the corrected binary to `/tmp` and ran `test.sh` with that on the `PATH` to verify — it passes cleanly. The source fix in `app/cluster/node.go` is what matters; a fresh build from source (as the Dockerfile does) will produce the passing binary.
